title: Logistic regression on frozen DINOv3 features for anomaly tags (pixltagger)
finding: On pixltagger's own labels a frozen-DINOv3 logistic probe put 56 to 74 true positives in its top 100 for malformed hand, foot and bad anatomy (chance would give 6 to 20), but every fit used about 1,200 or more labelled pictures, DINOv3 rather than PixlStash's CLIP vectors, and was never compared with the near-neighbour vote, so it cannot answer the 50-200-verdict question in #2678.

title: Out-of-fold probe ranking to surface pictures worth judging (pixltagger)
finding: In two blind games in the tagger repo, the pictures a held-out model ranked highest were confirmed no more often than a random batch (bad anatomy 1 of 9 vs 1 of 10; malformed eyes 8 of 47 = 17% vs 7 of 41 = 17%), and inside the ranked eyes batch the score did not order the positives (AUC 0.49), even though this model was much stronger than the classifier #2678 proposes.

title: Base-rate-relative thresholds for the near-neighbour vote
finding: Thresholds set relative to each tag's base rate cut the near-neighbour vote's remove-to-add skew with no real signal from 58x to 0.2-1.3x (a binomial model made now gives 63x and 0.24-1.45x), but no surviving number says whether a person confirms more of the vote's top 100, and pixltagger holds no trace of the experiment.

title: Learning curve of a CLIP logistic regression against the near-neighbour vote on held-out verdicts
finding: Fitted on 100 human verdicts, the CLIP logistic regression put clearly more confirmed pictures in its top 50 held-out pictures than the shipped near-neighbour vote on 7 of 20 tags (for example jewelry 65% against 34%), and was never clearly behind; but a neighbour vote restricted to the judged pictures matched it on every tag, so the gain comes from using the rejects, not from the linear boundary.

title: A person judges the classifier's top 100 against the near-neighbour's top 100
finding: When the owner judged each method's top 100 unjudged pictures, the classifier trained on 100 verdicts was clearly ahead of the shipped near-neighbour vote on neither tag tested: on hand it was clearly behind (83 of 100 confirmed against 94 of 98, p = 0.005), and on jewelry it was ahead but not clearly (39 of 74 against 28 of 76, p = 0.07), reversing on hand the 26-point lead idea 4 measured on already-judged pictures.
